MSFT.note: Acquired Activision Blizzard for ~$68.7 billion — largest gaming deal in history. Adds Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, Candy Crush, and King to Microsoft Gaming.

ATVI.note: Acquired by Microsoft (MSFT) for ~$68.7 billion. ATVI delisted from Nasdaq; gaming titles (Call of Duty, Candy Crush, World of Warcraft) now under Microsoft Gaming.

AVGO.note: Completed $69 billion acquisition of VMware. Rebranded enterprise software as 'VMware by Broadcom'; pivoted VMware to subscription model.

VMW.note: Acquired by Broadcom (AVGO) for ~$69 billion. VMware delisted from NYSE; cloud and subscription businesses absorbed into Broadcom's infrastructure software segment.

SHOP.note: Spun off Shopify Logistics (Deliverr + 6 River Systems) to Flexport for equity consideration, exiting warehousing and fulfillment operations to refocus on core commerce software.

GE.note: Spun off GE HealthCare (GEHC) as an independent Nasdaq-listed company on January 4, 2023.
Spun off GE Vernova (power & energy segment) as GEV on NYSE on April 2, 2024. GE retained as GE Aerospace — focused solely on jet engines and defense systems.

GEHC.note: GE HealthCare spun off from General Electric (GE) and began independent trading on Nasdaq as GEHC on January 4, 2023.

GEV.note: GE Vernova (power & energy segment) spun off from GE Aerospace and began trading on NYSE as GEV on April 2, 2024.

DIS.note: Completed full acquisition of Hulu by purchasing Comcast's remaining ~33% stake for $8.6 billion, giving Disney 100% ownership of the streaming platform.

HPE.note: Acquired Juniper Networks (JNPR) for ~$14 billion ($40/share cash). Deal closed February 2025 after extended DoJ antitrust review; adds AI-driven networking to HPE's hybrid-cloud portfolio.

JNPR.note: Acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) for ~$14 billion ($40/share cash). JNPR delisted from NYSE upon close in February 2025.

WBA.note: Walgreens Boots Alliance delisted from Nasdaq after agreeing to be taken private by Sycamore Partners for ~$10 billion. Previously removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average in February 2024.

UNH.note: CEO Andrew Witty resigned; guidance suspended amid elevated medical costs and a DoJ criminal fraud investigation into Medicare billing practices. Stock fell >50% from its peak. Brian Thompson, CEO of UnitedHealthcare, was fatally shot in December 2024.

CI.note: Cigna agreed to sell its Medicare Advantage business to Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC) for ~$3.7 billion, refocusing on commercial insurance and pharmacy benefits (Express Scripts).
